discovery: Geometric and topological phases in quantum mechanics (Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University, Israel, and Chapman University, USA

motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm) showed in 1959 that electromagnetic potentials have physical effects on electrons moving through field-free regions. Berry showed in 1984 that any quantum system carried adiabatically around a closed loop picks up a geometric phase. Together these results showed that quantum states carry a topological and geometric structure, holonomy, that goes beyond local forces. That idea runs through modern physics. The Aharonov-Bohm effect is routinely measured in mesoscopic rings and electron holography. Berry curvature underlies the anomalous and quantum Hall effects, the theory of electric polarization, topological insulators, graphene's pseudospin physics, Weyl semimetals and topological photonics. It is also central to proposals for topologically protected quantum computing. Berry's semiclassical work, including the Berry-Tabor conjecture on level statistics and random waves, further connected classical dynamics to quantum spectra. This is deep conceptual insight, confirmed across many experiments, that unifies disparate phenomena.
